title: Kernel Representation and Similarity Measure for Incomplete Data
summary: Measuring similarity between incomplete web-mining data is difficult because deletion and imputation can lose information or bias similarity estimates. The paper proposes a proximity kernel that uses equal-frequency binning, proximity assignment, one-hot/KME encodings, and a cascading intersection-union-global fallback to build a sparse kernel representation without explicit original-space imputation. Across 12 UCI clustering tasks with K-means, it obtains the highest average NMI (0.4245) and best or second-best results on 10 of 12 datasets, including 0.2289 on Hepatitis.

match_target.why: Honors the user hint exactly: Table 3, proximity kernel NMI on Hepatitis with K-means. Hepatitis is small (155 samples), so it is the cheapest central clustering result rather than a side ablation or scalability experiment.

tolerance.why: Rule 3: the paper reports no standard deviation for the target value; NMI is a bounded score printed in [0,1] on Hepatitis with 155 examples (<2000), so use 0.02 absolute points.

requirements.stmt: Assign each observed value to the nearest bin center, creating a Voronoi-like bin assignment.
requirements.quote: Given the bin centers {cj,1, ...,cj,nbins} for each feature j, we assign each observed value to its nearest center.

requirements.stmt: Encode each assigned bin as a one-hot vector and concatenate feature blocks into the complete representation z_i.

requirements.stmt: For missing features, first find samples matching the target sample in every observed feature bin, excluding the target itself.

requirements.stmt: If the intersection-based matching set is nonempty, estimate each missing feature block as the average encoding of matched samples.

requirements.stmt: If the intersection set is empty, relax to union-based matching over samples sharing at least one observed-feature bin and average their encodings.

requirements.stmt: Compute similarity as the inner product of concatenated representations averaged over the d features.
requirements.quote: This similarity measure has a probabilistic interpretation: it computes the expected probability that two samples fall into the same bin, averaged across all features.

requirements.stmt: Cluster the constructed representation vectors with K-means using the ground-truth number of classes.
requirements.quote: For fair comparison, we applied K-means with the number of clusters to the ground-truth number of classes.

requirements.stmt: Repeat each experiment 10 times and report the average result.
requirements.quote: Each experiment was conducted 10 times and report average results for stability.
